identification.summary: MITRE ATT&CK describes menuPass (tracked by Microsoft as Purple Typhoon) as a threat group active since at least 2006 [S1]. MITRE states that individual members are known to have acted in association with the Chinese Ministry of State Security's (MSS) Tianjin State Security Bureau and worked for the Huaying Haitai Science and Technology Development Company [S1].
identification.firstObserved: MITRE ATT&CK: active since at least 2006 [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Purple Typhoon. The record's alias list (APT10, menuPass, Stone Panda, BRONZE RIVERSIDE, Granite Taurus, Cicada, POTASSIUM and others) comes from the repository import (MITRE ATT&CK, MISP Galaxy, Microsoft, Google TI). This research pass could not re-verify it against a live Microsoft source. MirrorFace and TA410/Witchetty have separate records in this encyclopedia: vendors describe possible links to APT10 but track them as distinct clusters. Do not merge their activity into this profile.

attribution.basis: MITRE ATT&CK group description G0045, taken from this repository's ATT&CK import dated 2026-07-31 [S1]. The primary government documents behind this statement (the US DOJ indictment and the FBI release of December 2018, listed in the record's references) could not be opened in this pass.

capabilities.summary: MITRE ATT&CK associates 25 software entries with menuPass. They include custom or group-linked malware (ChChes, RedLeaves, UPPERCUT, SNUGRIDE, EvilGrab, Ecipekac, P8RAT, SodaMaster, FYAnti, HUI Loader), shared RATs (PlugX, PoisonIvy, QuasarRAT, Cobalt Strike) and dual-use or credential tools (Mimikatz, pwdump, PsExec, Impacket, AdFind, PowerSploit, certutil, esentutl) [S1].

diamond.adversary: PRC-linked operators; MITRE ties individual members to the MSS Tianjin State Security Bureau and Huaying Haitai Science and Technology Development Company [S1].
diamond.capability: Custom loaders and backdoors (ChChes, RedLeaves, UPPERCUT, Ecipekac, SodaMaster, P8RAT, HUI Loader) alongside PlugX, QuasarRAT, Cobalt Strike and credential-dumping tools [S1].
